title: Regularity and coordinate intersections on a permissible blowup chart
statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$. Fix $1\le r\le d$, a nonempty subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with $J\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}\ne\varnothing$, and a subset $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$. For $j\in J$, the standard chart of the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] of the ideal $(t_i:i\in J)$ is
$$A_j=R[ u_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{j\} ]/(t_i-t_j u_i\mid i\in J\setminus\{j\}),$$
with $u_i=t_i/t_j$; it is regular. If $B=V(t_1\cdots t_r)$, the reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of $B$ on this chart is the union of the coordinate hyperplanes $t_j=0$, $u_i=0$ for $i\in(J\setminus\{j\})\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}$, and $t_k=0$ for $k\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\setminus J$. At every point these hyperplanes have local equations among a regular system of parameters; every intersection of a subset of them is empty or regular and has codimension equal to the size of the subset. If $M=V(t_i:i\in J)$ and $H=V(\prod_{i\in I}t_i)$ (empty product means $H=\varnothing$), the reduced inverse image of $H\cup M$ is the union of the exceptional hyperplane $t_j=0$ and the strict transforms [def-nagata-strict-transform] of the components $V(t_i)$, $i\in I$. On this chart the strict transform of $V(t_i)$ is the coordinate hyperplane $u_i=0$ if $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$, is empty if $i=j$, and is the coordinate hyperplane $t_i=0$ if $i\notin J$. Scheme-theoretic intersections and codimension use [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: Permute the parameter system with $t_j$ first. The regular-sequence assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] and [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] identify the stated quotient with the standard chart, sending $u_i$ to $t_i/t_j$. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-algebra-regular] to this quotient to obtain its regularity.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: In $A_j$, the pullback of $t_i$ is $t_j$, $t_j u_i$, or $t_i$ according as $i=j$, $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$, or $i\notin J$. Thus $\prod_{i=1}^r t_i=t_j^{|J\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}|}\prod_{i\in(J\setminus\{j\})\cap\{1,\ldots,r\}}u_i\prod_{k\leq r,\ k\notin J}t_k$. The exponent is positive. A prime contains this product exactly when it contains a displayed factor, so reduction gives precisely the asserted reduced union [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-parameter-blowup-coordinate-quotients] to $A_j$, regular by Step 1. The boundary equations are a subfamily of its labelled coordinates. Its parameter assertion applies simultaneously to every equation vanishing at a chosen prime. Its quotient and dimension formulas, with $c$ the number of chosen labels, give regularity and codimension for every scheme-theoretic intersection; a unit equation gives an empty local intersection.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: The extended center is $(t_j)$ by [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal], so [def-nagata-strict-transform] takes schematic closure from $D(t_j)$. For $i=j$ the off-center hyperplane is empty. For $i\in J\setminus\{j\}$ its equation there is $u_i$, and for $i\notin J$ it is $t_i$. Write this equation as $q$. By [lem-trf-chart-coordinate-nonzerodivisors], multiplication by $t_j$ on $A_j/(q)$ is injective. Hence if $t_j^n x\in(q)$ then $x\in(q)$, by $n$ successive cancellations. The localization kernel is therefore exactly $(q)$, giving schematic closure $V(q)$, not just its support.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9 coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121

proof.text: For $H\cup M$, the inverse-image support is the exceptional $V(t_j)$ together with the pullbacks of $V(t_i)$ for $i\in I$. The substitution in Step 2 and the strict equations in Step 4 give the asserted reduced union. For $I=\varnothing$ only $V(t_j)$ remains. These are restrictions of the intrinsic inverse image and schematic closure on the same blowup, so agree on overlaps. This completes every clause.

mathlib_searches.query: In a regular local coordinate chart, blowing up an ideal generated by a subset of parameters gives regular affine charts and the reduced total transform of coordinate hyperplanes is a normal crossings divisor; a strict coordinate sub-boundary plus the exceptional divisor is strict normal crossings.
